topics.label: Introduction to inflammation initiation and resolution
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture as an integration of previously introduced immune cells and molecules.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate immunity detects infection and damage through suitable molecular patterns and appropriately positioned, germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor pathways and inflammatory signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how specific pattern recognition systems translate microbial or damage signals into immune responses.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how activated sentinel cells initiate inflammation that brings circulating leukocytes to the infection site.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the lymphatic system enables infection signals from tissues to reach lymph nodes and initiate adaptive immunity.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how excessive inflammatory activation becomes a life-threatening systemic response.

topics.label: Passive and active resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammation subsides through withdrawal of inflammatory stimulation and active inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what happens when inflamed tissue is repaired or remains chronically inflamed because the underlying problem cannot be eliminated.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture on complement
topics.groupedBecause: The closing ends the lecture and identifies complement as the subject of the next session.
